en: Being is the indeterminate immediacy; it is free of determinateness against essence, as well as of every determinateness which it might be able to receive within itself.
This reflectionless being is being such as it is immediately only by itself.
zh: 存在乃是不确定的直接者；它既免于与本质相对的规定性，也免于它自身之内所能接受的任何规定性。
这个无反思的存在乃是这样一种存在：它直接地仅就它自身而言。

en: Because it is indeterminate, it is qualityless being; but in itself the character of indeterminateness accrues to it only in contrast with the determinate or the qualitative.
To being in general, however, determinate being stands opposed as such; and thereby it is precisely its indeterminateness which constitutes its quality.
It will therefore be shown that the first being is determinate in itself, and thereby
zh: 因为它是不确定的，所以它是无质的存在；但自在地看，不确定性的性状只有在同规定者或质的规定相对时，才归属于它。
然而对存在一般而言，规定的存在作为这样的东西与之相对立；而正是在这一意义上，它的不确定性本身就构成了它的质。
因此将会表明：最初的存在自在地是规定者，并且由此

en: Secondly, that it passes over into determinate existence, into existence; but that this as finite being sublates itself and into the infinite relation of being to itself,
zh: 第二，它过渡到定在，过渡到定在；但这一作为有限的存在自我扬弃，并且过渡到存在与自身之无限的关系，

en: Thirdly, into being-for-self.
zh: 第三，它过渡到自为存在。

en: Being, pure being, — without any further determination.
In its indeterminate immediacy it is only equal to itself and not unequal towards the other; it has no diversity within itself or towards the outside.
Through any determination or content which were distinguished in it or through which it would be set as distinguished from an other, it would not be maintained in its purity.
It is pure indeterminateness and emptiness.
— There is nothing in it to be intuited, if intuition can be spoken of here; or it is only this pure, empty intuition itself.
There is just as little to be thought in it, or it is likewise only this empty thinking.
Being, the indeterminate immediacy, is in truth nothing and not more nor less than nothing.
zh: 存在，纯粹的存在，——没有任何进一步的规定。
在其不确定的直接性中，它只与自己相等，对其他者也并不相异；它自身之内没有相异，向外也没有相异。
通过某种在它之内被区别开的、或通过它被设定为与某个他者相区别的规定或内容，它便不能保持其纯粹性。
它是纯粹的不确定性与空虚。
——在这里若可以谈直观的话，其中便没有任何东西可被直观；或者说，它本身无非就是这种纯粹的、空的直观。
同样地，其中也没有任何东西可以被思维；或者说，它同样无非就是这种空的思维。
存在，即不确定的直接者，实际上是无，既不多于无，也不少于无。

en: Nothing, pure nothing; it is simple equality with itself, complete emptiness, absence of determination and of content; non-difference within itself.
— Insofar as intuition or thinking can be mentioned here, it makes a difference whether something or nothing is intuited or thought.

Intuition or thinking of nothing therefore does have a meaning; the two are distinguished, so that nothing (exists) in our intuition or thinking; or rather what is there is the empty intuition and thinking itself, the same empty intuition or thinking as the pure being.
— Nothing is therefore the same determination, or rather the same absence of determination, and thus altogether the same as the pure being.
zh: 无，纯无；它是与自身的简单相等，完全的空虚，规定与内容的不在场；在自身之内的无差别。
——在这里若能谈直观或思维，那么被直观或被思维的是某物还是无，就构成一种差别。
因此，对无的直观或对无的思维确实具有一种意义；两者是被区别开来的，因而在我们的直观或思维中（存在）着无；或者毋宁说，在那里所存在的正是空的直观与思维本身，就是与纯粹存在同一个空的直观或思维。
——因此，无乃是同一的规定，或者毋宁说乃是同一的无规定，因而总之与纯粹存在是同一个东西。

12.en: a. The Unity of Being and Nothing

en: Pure being and pure nothing are therefore the same.
What truth is, is neither being nor nothing, but that being has passed over into nothing and nothing into being — not passes over, but has passed over.

But just as little is truth their non-difference, but rather that they are not the same, that they are absolutely different, yet at the same time undivided and inseparable, and that each immediately disappears in its opposite.

Their truth is therefore this movement of the immediate disappearance of the one into the other: becoming; a movement in which both are different, but through a difference which has likewise immediately dissolved itself.
zh: 因此，纯粹的存在与纯粹的无是同一个。
真理者既不是存在，也不是无，而是：存在已过渡到无，无已过渡到存在——不是将要过渡，而是已经过渡了。
但真理同样也不是它们的无差别，而是：它们不是同一个，它们是绝对有差别的，但同样又是未分开的、不可分离的，并且每一个都直接地消失在其对立面之中。
因此，它们的真理就是这一个在另一个之中的直接消失的运动：即生成；这是一场运动，在其中两者是有差别的，但却是借助一个同样直接地自行消解了的差别。

en: Nothing is usually opposed to the something; but the something is already a determinate being which differs from another something; so too the nothing opposed to the something, the nothing of some something or other, is a determinate nothing.
But here the nothing is to be taken in its indeterminate simplicity.

— If one were to hold it to be more correct that instead of the nothing it is non-being which is opposed to being, then in view of the result there would be nothing to object to; for the relation to being is contained in non-being; non-being is both, being and the negation of it, expressed in one, the nothing as it is in becoming.

But what is at issue in the first place is not the form of opposition, i.e. at the same time of relation, but the abstract, immediate negation, the nothing purely by itself, the relationless no, — which, if one wishes, one could also express through the mere not.
zh: 无通常是与某物相对立的；但某物已经是一个被规定的存在者，它与另一个某物相区别；因此，与某物相对立的那个无、某个某物的那个无，也是一个被规定的无。
但在这里，这个无须在它不确定的单纯性上来把握。
——如果人们认为与存在相对立的应当不是无而是非存在，那么顾及结果也就没有什么可以反对的了；因为与存在的关系是包含在非存在之中的；非存在把两者——存在以及对存在的否定——统一表达在一个东西中，那就是如生成之中的那个无。
但首先问题不在于对立的形式，即同时也是关系的形式，而在于抽象的、直接的否定，即纯粹自在的无、无关系的否定，——如果人们愿意，也可以用单纯的「非」来表达它。

en: The Eleatics were the first to have the simple thought of pure being — Parmenides in particular, as the absolute and as the only truth — and to have expressed it in the surviving fragments of his works, with the pure enthusiasm of a thinking which for the first time comprehends itself in its absolute abstraction: only being is being, and nothing is not at all.
— In oriental systems, essentially in Buddhism, the nothing, the empty, is known to be the absolute principle.

— The profound Heraclitus raised against that simple and one-sided abstraction the higher, more total concept of becoming, and said: being is no more than nothing, or also: everything flows, that is: everything is becoming.

— The popular sayings, particularly oriental ones, that everything which is has the seed of its passing away in its birth itself, that death conversely is the entrance into new life, express at bottom the same union of being and nothing.

But these expressions have a substratum in which the transition occurs; being and nothing are held apart in time, are represented in it alternately, but are not thought in their abstraction, and hence not in such a way that they are the same in and for themselves.
zh: 纯粹存在的单纯思想，首先是爱利亚学派具有的，尤其是巴门尼德：他把它当作绝对者、当作唯一的真理，而且是在他遗存的残篇中，以那种第一次在其绝对抽象中把握住自身的思维之纯粹热情表达出来的：唯有存在是存在着的，而无则根本不存在。
——在东方的体系中，尤其是在佛教中，众所周知，无与空乃是绝对原则。
——深沉的赫拉克利特针对那种单纯而片面的抽象提出了更高的、总体的生成概念，并说：存在并不比无更多，或者说：一切皆流变，这就是说：一切都是生成。
——那些通俗的、尤其是东方的格言——凡存在者，其消逝的种子就在它自身的诞生之中，而反过来死亡乃是进入新生命的入口——归根到底，表达的都是存在与无的统一。
但这些表达有一个基底，转换就在这基底中发生；存在与无是在时间中被分开的，在时间中交替地被表象，而不是在其抽象中被思维，因而也不是自在且自为地就成为同一个东西。

en: “Ex nihilo nihil fit” is one of the propositions to which great significance was attributed in metaphysics.

In it one may see either only the empty tautology: nothing is nothing; or if becoming were to have a real significance in it, then rather — since only nothing becomes from nothing — there is in fact no becoming in it, for nothing remains nothing in it.
Becoming contains that nothing should not remain nothing, but rather pass over into its other, into being.

— If the later, especially Christian metaphysics rejected the proposition that nothing comes from nothing, then it asserted a transition from nothing into being; however synthetic or merely representational it took this proposition to be, there is contained even in the most imperfect union a point in which being and nothing meet and their difference disappears.

— Its proper significance the proposition “out of nothing comes nothing, nothing is simply nothing” has through its contrast with becoming in general, and thereby also with the creation of the world out of nothing.

Those who assert the proposition “nothing is simply nothing”, even zealously advocating it, are unconscious of the fact that in doing so they side with the abstract pantheism of the Eleatics, and in fact also with the Spinozist one.
The philosophical view for which “being is only being, nothing is only nothing” holds as a principle deserves the name of an identity system; this abstract identity is the essence of pantheism.
zh: 无中不能生有（Ex nihilo nihil fit）是形而上学中被赋予重大意义的命题之一。
在它里面人们要么只看到空洞的同义反复：无就是无；要么，如果生成在它里面应当具有真正的意义，那么毋宁说，由于只不过是无从无产生，因而它里面实际上并没有生成，因为无在其中仍然是无。
生成包含着这一点：无双复停留为无，而是过渡到它的他者，即过渡到存在。
——如果后来的、尤其是基督教的形而上学弃绝了「无从无产生」这一命题，那么它就断定有一个从无到存在的过渡；无论它把这一命题当作综合的、还是仅仅当作表象的，即便在最不完善的统一中，也仍然包含着一个点，在这一点上存在与无相遇，而它们的差别消失。
——命题「无中不产生有，无就是无」由于与生成总体的对立、从而也与从无创造世界相对立，才获得它本来的重要性。
那些主张「无就是无」这一命题的人——甚至还热心地为它辩护——并没有意识到：他们这样做就等于附和了爱利亚学派的抽象泛神论，实质上也附和了斯宾诺莎的泛神论。
那种把「存在只是存在，无只是无」当作原则的哲学观点，配得上「同一性体系」这个名称；这种抽象的同一性正是泛神论的本质。

en: If the result that being and nothing are the same strikes one as striking or paradoxical in itself, then no further notice need be taken of this; rather one should be surprised at that astonishment which shows itself as so new in philosophy and forgets that in this science quite different determinations occur than in ordinary consciousness and in the so-called common human understanding, which is not precisely the healthy understanding but equally the understanding elevated to abstractions and to the faith — or rather superstition — in abstractions.
It would not be difficult to show this unity of being and nothing in every example, in every actual thing or thought.

What was said above of immediacy and mediation — the latter a relation of one to the other, and thereby containing negation — must be said of being and nothing: that there is nowhere in heaven and on earth anything which is not both.
Being and nothing, contained in themselves.

Of course, since here the talk is of some something or other and of what is actual, those determinations are no longer present in the complete untruth in which they are as being and nothing, but in a further determination, and are taken, for example, as the positive and the negative: the former the posited, reflected being, the latter the posited, reflected nothing; but the positive and the negative contain that being and that nothing respectively as their abstract ground.
— Thus in God himself the quality, activity, creation, power, etc. essentially contain the determination of the negative; they are a bringing forth of an other.
But an empirical elucidation of that claim through examples would be quite superfluous here.

Since this unity of being and nothing now lies at the foundation as the first truth for good and all, and constitutes the element of everything that follows, so apart from becoming itself all the more remote logical determinations — existence, quality, and in general all the concepts of philosophy — are examples of this unity.

— But the so-called common or healthy human understanding may be referred to the attempt, insofar as it rejects the indivisibility of being and nothing, to seek out an example in which one might find the one separated from the other (the something from the limit, the limit or the infinite, God as just mentioned, from activity).

Only the empty thought-things, being and nothing themselves, are these separated ones; and it is they who are preferred by that understanding to the truth, to the indivisibility of both, which is everywhere present before us.
zh: 如果「存在与无是同一个东西」这一结果本身显得突兀或悖谬，那么对此无须再多留意；毋宁说，人们反倒应当对那种惊异感到惊异：它在哲学中显得如此新奇，并且忘掉了在这门科学中所出现的规定与日常意识、与所谓普通的常识（那与其说是健康的知性，不如说同样是那种被提升到抽象、且被提升到对抽象的信仰或毋宁说迷信的知性）中所出现的规定全然不同。
在每一个例子、在每一件现实之物或每一个思想中指出存在与无的这种统一，并不困难。
上面关于直接性与中介（后者是一种彼此间的关系，因而包含着否定）所说的，同样也必须关于存在与无来说：天上地下没有任何东西不是二者兼有。
存在与无，在自身中包含着。
当然，既然这里所谈的是某物和某个现实者，那么那些规定就不再以它们作为存在与无时所处的完全非真状态而存在，而是处在一种进一步的规定中；例如，它们被理解为肯定与否定：前者是被设定的、被反思的存在，后者是被设定的、被反思的无；但肯定与否定分别把那存在、那无作为自己的抽象根据。
——因此在上帝自身之中，质、活动、创造、力量等等，本质上都包含着否定的规定——它们乃是对一个他者的产生。
但在这里，用例子来经验地诠释那一断言是完全多余的。
既然存在与无的这种统一现在作为最初的真理一劳永逸地奠定了根据，并构成一切后继者的要素，那么除了生成自身之外，一切更遥远的逻辑规定——定在、质，以及总而言之哲学的一切概念——都是这一统一的例证。
——但那自称为普通或健康的常识，若它拒斥存在与无的不可分离性，则尽可被提醒去尝试：找出一个例子，在其中人们可以把一方与另一方分开（把某物同界限、界限或无限者——上帝，如刚才所提到的——同活动分开）。
只有那些空的思想物——存在与无自身——才是这些被分开的东西；而恰恰是它们被那种知性选取，取代了真理、取代了二者的不可分离性，而这不可分性处处都呈现在我们面前。

en: One cannot intend to wish to meet the confusions into which ordinary consciousness is thrown by such a logical proposition in every direction, for they are inexhaustible.
Only a few can be mentioned.

One reason for such confusions, among others, is that the consciousness brings to such an abstract logical proposition representations of a concrete something, and forgets that the talk is not of such a something but only of the pure abstractions of being and nothing, and that these alone are to be held fast.
zh: 人们不可能既有意图、又有意愿，去在一切方面应对普通意识在这样一条逻辑命题上所陷入的那些混乱，因为这些混乱是无穷无尽的。
只能提到其中若干个。
这类混乱的一个原因——此外还有很多——在于：意识带着关于具体某物的表象来面对这样一条抽象的逻辑命题，并且忘掉了：这里所谈的并不是这样的某物，而只是存在与无的纯粹抽象，并且唯有这些抽象才应当被把握住。

en: Being and non-being are the same; thus it is the same whether I am or am not, whether this house is or is not, whether these hundred thalers are in my state of property or not.
— This conclusion, or application of that proposition, changes its meaning completely.
The proposition contains the pure abstractions of being and nothing; but the application makes a determinate being and a determinate nothing of them.
Yet, as has been said, it is not of determinate being that we are speaking here.
A determinate, a finite being, is such a being as relates itself to something other; it is a content which, in the relation of necessity, stands with other content, with the whole world.

In view of the mutually determining interconnection of the whole, metaphysics could make the — in the ground tautological — assertion that if a dust particle were destroyed the whole universe would collapse.

In the instances which are brought against the proposition under discussion, something appears as not indifferent whether it be or not be — not for the sake of its being or non-being, but for the sake of its content, which connects it with something other.

If a determinate content, any determinate existence, is presupposed, then this existence, because it is determinate, stands in manifold relation to other content; for it, it is not indifferent whether a certain other content with which it stands in relation is or is not; for only through such a relation is it essentially that which it is.

The same is the case in representing (since we take non-being in the more determinate sense of representing against actuality), in whose connection the being or the absence of a content which is represented as determinate in relation to something other is not indifferent.
zh: 存在与非存在是同一个东西；因此，我存在还是不存在是同一个回事，这座房子存在还是不存在是同一个回事，这一百塔勒尔是在我的财产状态之中还是不在，也是同一个回事。
——这一推论，或者说对那一命题的应用，完全改变了它的意义。
这一命题包含着存在与无的纯粹抽象；但这一应用却从中造出一个被规定的存在和一个被规定的无。
然而，如前所述，这里所谈的并不是被规定的存在。
一个被规定的、有限的存在是这样的存在：它与别的东西相关联；它是一个内容，在必然性的关系中与别的内容、与整个世界处于同一之中。
鉴于整体中相互规定的联系，形而上学得以提出那——在根本上是重言式的——断言：如果一粒尘埃被毁灭，整个宇宙就会崩塌。
在那些被提出来反对所论命题的例证中，某种东西显得并非无关紧要：它存在还是不存在——这并不是出于它存在或非存在的缘故，而是出于其内容的缘故，因为这一内容把它与别的东西联结在一起。
如果预设了一个规定着的内容、任何一个规定着的定在，那么这一定在由于是规定着的，就与别的内容处于多方面的关系之中；对它来说，某个与它处于关系之中的别的内容是存在还是不存在，并非无关紧要；因为唯有通过这样的关系，它才在本质上就是它所是的东西。
在表象中情形也是一样的（因为我们在表象这一较为规定的意义下，把非存在与现实性相对地加以把握），在表象的关联中，那个被表象为在与其他者的关系中已获规定的内容的存在或其缺失，并不是无关紧要的。

en: This consideration contains what constitutes a main moment in the Kantian critique of the ontological proof of the existence of God, upon which, however, here only regard is paid to the difference between being and nothing in general and between determinate being or non-being which occurs in it.

— As is well known, in that so-called proof the concept of an essence was presupposed, to which all reality belongs, and thus existence too; and existence was likewise assumed to be one of those realities.

The Kantian critique held itself above all to the point that existence or being (which is here taken to be equivalent) is no property and no real predicate, i.e. not a concept of something which could come in addition to the concept of a thing.7 — By this Kant means to say that being is no determination of content.

Thus, he continues, the possible contains no more than the actual; a hundred actual thalers contain nothing more than a hundred possible ones; — namely, the former have no other determination of content than the latter.

For this content considered in isolation, it is indeed indifferent whether it is or is not; there lies in it no difference of being or non-being, this difference does not touch it at all; the hundred thalers do not become less if they are not, nor more if they are.
A difference must first come from somewhere else.
— “But”, Kant recalls, “in my state of property there is more in a hundred actual thalers than in the mere concept of them (i.e. of their possibility).”

For the object is not contained in my concept merely analytically when it is actual, but comes in synthetically to my concept (which is a determination of my state), without these thought-of hundred thalers themselves being increased in the least by this being outside my concept.”
zh: 这一考察所包含的，正是康德对上帝的存在的本体论证明之批判中的一个主要环节；不过在这里，人们只顾及其中出现的存在与无的差别、以及被规定的存在或非存在这一差别。
——众所周知，在那个所谓的证明中预设了一个本质的概念，一切实在性都归属于它，存在也因而归属于它；而存在同样地被假定为那些实在性之一。
康德的批判主要紧抓住这一点：存在或存在（在这里二者被视为同义）并不是一种属性，也不是一个实在的谓词，也就是说，并不是关于某种可以附加到某物概念之上的东西的概念。7——康德借此想说，存在并不是一种内容规定。
于是他继续说：可能者并不比现实者包含更多；一百个现实的塔勒尔并不比一百个可能的塔勒尔多包含丝毫；——也就是说，前者并不具有与后者不同的内容规定。
对于被孤立地考察的这些内容来说，存在还是不存在的确无关紧要；在它之中不存在存在与非存在的差别，这一差别根本完全没有触及它；这一百塔勒尔在不存在时不会变少，在存在时也不会变多。
差别必须先从别处而来。
——「但是」，康德提醒说，「在我的财产状态中，一百个现实的塔勒尔比关于它们的单纯概念（即关于它们的可能性）包含着更多。」
因为就现实性而言，对象并非仅仅被分析地包含在我的概念之中，而是综合地添加到我的概念上（这个概念是我状态的一种规定），并且这些被想到的一百塔勒尔本身，并不因这一在我的概念之外的存在而增加丝毫。」

en: Two states are presupposed here — staying with the Kantian expressions, which are not without confused clumsiness: the one which Kant calls the concept, understanding by that the representation, and another, the state of property.

For the one as for the other, for the capacity as for the representing, a hundred thalers are a determination of content, or they come synthetically to such a one, as Kant expresses it; I as possessor of a hundred thalers or as non-possessor of them, or also I as representing a hundred thalers to myself or not representing them, is indeed a different content.

More generally put: the abstractions of being and nothing both cease to be abstractions when they receive a determinate content; being is then reality, the determinate being of 100 thalers; nothing is negation, the determinate non-being of the same.
This determination of content itself, the hundred thalers, taken also abstractly by themselves, is in the one just as unchangedly the same as in the other.

But further, when being is taken as a state of property, the hundred thalers enter into relation with a state, and for this state such determinateness as they are is not indifferent; their being or non-being is only a change; they are transported into the sphere of determinate existence.

If therefore it is urged against the unity of being and nothing that it is after all not indifferent whether this and that (the 100 thalers) is or is not, then it is an illusion that we push the difference out onto being and non-being alone, whether I have the hundred thalers or have them not; — an illusion which, as has been shown, rests on the one-sided abstraction which leaves out the determinate existence that is present in such examples and holds fast to being and non-being alone, just as conversely it transforms the abstract being and nothing which is to be comprehended into a determinate being and nothing, into an existence.
Only determinate existence contains the real difference between being and nothing, namely a something and an other.
— This real difference is what floats before the representation, instead of the abstract being and pure nothing and their merely intended difference.
zh: 这里预设了两种状态——为留在康德的那些说法上，它们并非没有混乱的笨拙——：其一，是康德称作概念的东西，其中应当理解为表象；其二，是财产状态。
无论对于其一还是对于其二，无论对于能力还是对于表象，一百塔勒尔都是一种内容规定，或者按照康德的说法，它们是综合地添加到这样一种内容规定上的；而我作为一百塔勒尔的占有者或作为它们的非占有者，或者我作为向自己表象一百塔勒尔者或不表象它们者，确实是一个不同的内容。
更一般地说：存在与无这两个抽象一旦获得规定着的内容，就都不再是抽象了；这时存在就是实在性，即一百塔勒尔的规定着的存在；而无就是否定，即同样这些塔勒尔的规定着的非存在。
这一内容规定本身，即这一百塔勒尔，即便把它抽象地单独加以考察，在前者中也与在后者中毫无变化地是同一个东西。
但进一步说，当存在被当作财产状态来把握时，这一百塔勒尔就与一个状态进入关系之中，而对于这个状态来说，它们所是的那种规定性并非无关紧要；它们的存在或非存在只是一种变化；它们被移入了定在的领域。
因此，如果有人针对存在与无的统一坚持说：这一方与那一方（那一百塔勒尔）存在还是不存在毕竟不是无关紧要的，那么认为我们只是把差别推到存在与非存在上去、只是问有没有这一百塔勒尔，这是一种幻觉；——正如已经指出的，这种幻觉建立在片面的抽象之上：这种抽象撇下了在这类例子中现成存在的规定着的定在，只抓住存在与非存在；反过来，它又把那个应当被把握的抽象的存在与无，转化为一个规定着的存在与无、一个定在。
唯有定在才包含存在与无的实在的差别，即某物与他者。
——这一实在的差别悬在表象之前，取代了抽象的存在与纯粹的无以及它们那仅仅被意指的差别。

en: As Kant expresses it, ‹through existence something comes into the context of the entire experience‹; ‹we thereby gain one more object of perception, but our concept of the object is thereby not increased‹.

— This means, as emerges from what has been explained, so much: through existence — essentially because a something is determinate existence — it comes into connection with something other and, among other things, with a perceiver.
— The concept of the hundred thalers, says Kant, is not increased through perceiving.
The concept here means the hundred thalers represented in isolation, noted above.

In this isolated way they are indeed an empirical content, but cut off, without connection and determinateness against the other; the form of identity with itself deprives them of the relation to the other and makes it indifferent whether they are perceived or not.

But this so-called concept of the hundred thalers is a false concept; the form of the simple relation to itself does not belong to such a limited, finite content itself; it is a form imposed upon it and lent to it by the subjective understanding; a hundred thalers are not something related to itself, but something changeable and perishable.
zh: 按照康德的说法，‹通过存在，某种东西进入全部经验的关联之中‹；‹我们由此多得到一个知觉对象，但我们关于该对象的概念并不因此有所增加‹。
——这意思，按照已经作出的诠释，正是：借助存在——本质上是由于某物乃是规定着的存在——某物便与别的东西处于关联之中，并且除了别的之外，也与一个知觉者处于关联之中。
——康德说，一百塔勒尔的概念并不因知觉而有所增加。
这里的概念指的是前面提到的、被孤立地表象出来的一百塔勒尔。
以这种孤立的方式，它们固然是一个经验的内容，但却是被截断的，没有关联，也没有对他者的规定性；与自身同一性的形式剥夺了它们对他者的关系，并使它们被知觉与否都无关紧要。
但这个所谓一百塔勒尔的概念是一个错误的概念；单纯地与自身相关的形式并不属于这样有限的内容本身；它是主观的知性强加于它并借给它的形式；一百塔勒尔并不是一个与自身相关的东西，而是一个可变的、易逝的东西。

en: The thinking or representing in which only a determinate being, determinate existence, is present must be referred back to the beginning of science mentioned above, which Parmenides made, who clarified and elevated his representing, and thereby also the representing of posterity, into the pure thought, being as such, and thereby created the element of science.
— What the first is in science has had to show itself historically as the first.

And the Eleatic one or being we have to take as the first of the knowledge of thought; water and suchlike material principles may well be the universal, but as materials they are not pure thoughts; the numbers are neither the first simple nor the one that stays by itself, but a thought entirely external to itself.
zh: 那种其中只浮现出一个被规定的存在、一个定在的思维或表象，必须被指回到上面提到的那个科学开端；那开端是巴门尼德所作的：他把自己的表象、从而也把后人的表象，提炼并提升为纯粹的思想、作为这样的存在，并由此创造了科学的要素。
——科学中的第一者，历史上必须表现为第一者。
而爱利亚学派的一或存在，我们应当视为关于思维之知识的第一者；水以及诸如此类的物质原则固然可以是普遍者，但作为物质它们并不是纯粹的思想；数字既不是第一个单纯者，也不是那个保持在自身之中的者，而是一个完全外在于自身的思想。

en: The rejection of the particular finite being to being as such in its quite abstract universality is to be regarded as the very first theoretical, and even also practical, requirement.

For if a sublation of the hundred thalers is made, that it makes a difference in my state of property whether I have them or not, still more whether I am or am not, whether something other is or is not, then — without mentioning that there will be states of property for which such a possession of a hundred thalers will be indifferent — one may be reminded that man is to raise himself in his disposition to this abstract universality, in which it is indeed indifferent to him whether the hundred thalers, whatever quantitative relation to his state of property they may have, are or are not, just as much as it is indifferent to him whether he is or is not, i.e. whether he is in finite life or not (for a state, determinate being, is meant) and so forth.
— even should si fractus illabatur orbis, impavidum ferient ruinae, a Roman has said, and the Christian is to find himself still more in this indifference.
zh: 从特殊的有限存在退回作为这样的、处于其完全抽象的普遍性中的存在，既应当看作最初的理论要求，甚至也看作实践的要求。

因为，如果人们作出一番对一百塔勒尔的扬弃，主张在我的财产状态中我有没有它们、乃至我存在还是不存在、别的东西存在还是不存在，毕竟是有差别的，那么——且不说会有这样的财产状态，在其中对一百塔勒尔的这种占有是无关紧要的——人们可以提醒说：人应当在自己的心态中把自己提升到这种抽象的普遍性；在这种普遍性中，那一百塔勒尔——无论它们与他的财产状态具有何种量的关系——存在还是不存在，对它确实无关紧要；同样，他存在还是不存在，即他在有限的生命中还是不在有限的生命中，也对他无关紧要（这里所指的是一种状态、一种被规定的存在），如此等等。
——即便 si fractus illabatur orbis, impavidum ferient ruinae（纵然世界崩裂、废墟坠落也砸不倒那无畏者），一位罗马人这样说过；而基督徒则更应当发现自己置身于这样一种无关紧要之中。

en: The immediate connection in which the elevation above the hundred thalers and finite things in general stands to the ontological proof and to the Kantian critique of it quoted above still has to be indicated.

This critique has made itself generally plausible through its popular example; who does not know that a hundred actual thalers are different from a hundred merely possible ones, that they make a difference in my state of property?

Because this diversity shows itself in the hundred thalers, the concept, i.e. the determination of content as empty possibility, and being are different from each other; so too God’s concept is different from his being, and just as little as I can derive the actuality of the hundred thalers from their possibility, so little can I “pick out” the existence of God from the concept of God; but this picking out of the existence of God from his concept is what the ontological proof consists in.
Now if it is indeed true that the concept of being is different from being, then God is still more different from the hundred thalers and the other finite things.

It is the definition of finite things that in them concept and being, concept and reality, soul and body, are separable, that they are thereby perishable and mortal; the abstract definition of God is, on the contrary, precisely this, that his concept and his being are undivided and inseparable.

The true critique of the categories and of reason is precisely this: to comprehend this difference and to hold it back, to prevent the determinations and relations of the finite from being applied to God.
zh: 还应当指出：对一百塔勒尔以及一切有限事物的提升，与上面所引的本体论证明及其康德批判之间所具有的那种直接联结。
这一批判通过它那个通俗的例子而取得普遍的合理性；谁不知道一百个现实的塔勒尔不同于一百个仅仅可能的塔勒尔，不知道它们在我的财产状态中构成差别呢？
既然这种相异在这一百塔勒尔上显现出来，那么概念、即作为空可能性的内容规定，与存在就是彼此不同的；同样，上帝的概念也与他的存在不同；而且正如我无法从一百塔勒尔的可能性中推出它们的现实性，同样我也无法从上帝的概念中「挑出」他的存在；而从上帝的概念中挑出上帝的存在，正是本体论证明的所在。
如果「概念与存在相异」这件事确实成立，那么上帝与一百塔勒尔以及其他有限事物就更加相异。
有限事物的定义乃是：在它们之中概念与存在、概念与实在性、灵魂与身体是可分离的，因而它们是易逝的、有死的；相反，上帝的抽象定义恰恰在于：他的概念与他的存在是未分的、不可分离的。
对范畴与理性的真正批判恰恰在于：理解这一差别并把它挡开，不让有限者的规定与关系被应用到上帝身上。

en: A further reason is to be adduced which helps to explain the aversion to the proposition on being and nothing; this reason is that the expression of the result which emerges from the consideration of being and nothing is imperfect in the proposition “being and nothing is one and the same”.
The accent is laid preferably on the being-one-and-the-same, as in judgement in general, in which the predicate first says what the subject is.

The sense therefore seems to be that the difference were denied, whereas it occurs at the same time immediately in the proposition; for it speaks out both determinations, being and nothing, and contains them as different.
— It cannot at the same time be meant that one should abstract from them and hold fast only to the unity.
This sense would itself declare itself one-sided, since that from which one is to abstract is nevertheless present in the proposition and named there.

— Insofar then as the proposition “being and nothing is the same” expresses the identity of these determinations, but at the same time in truth contains them both as different, it contradicts itself and dissolves itself.
If we hold this more closely fixed, then here a proposition is posited which, considered more nearly, has the movement of vanishing through itself.
But thereby what is to constitute its proper content, namely becoming, happens to it itself.
zh: 还必须提出另一个理由，它有助于说明对关于存在与无这一命题的反感；这个理由就是：从对存在与无的考察中所得出的结果，用「存在与无是同一个东西」这一命题来表达，是不完善的。
重音尤其落在「是同一个」上，如同在一般判断中那样：在判断里，谓词首先说出主体是什么。
因此其意义似乎在于：差别被否认了，然而它同时又直接地出现在这一命题中；因为这一命题说出两个规定——存在与无——并且把它们作为有差别的包含着。
——同时也不能被理解为：应当从它们抽象出来而只抓住统一。
这种意义本身就会表明自己是片面的，因为那应当被抽象掉的东西毕竟还是在命题之中，并且在其中被指名的。
——就「存在与无是同一个东西」这一命题说出这些规定的同一性、而同时在真理中又把两者作为相异的包含着而言，它便自相矛盾，并且自行消解。
若把这一点更切近地把握住，那么这里所设定的是一个命题：从更切近的考察来看，它具有着通过自身而消失的运动。
但由此，那本应构成其真正内容的东西、即生成，便在它自身上发生了。

en: The proposition thus contains the result; it is this in itself.
The circumstance however which is to be indicated here is the defect that the result is not itself expressed in the proposition; it is an external reflection which recognises it in the proposition.

— Here one must at once make the general remark that the proposition, in the form of a judgement, is not suited to express speculative truths; acquaintance with this circumstance would be fitted to remove many misunderstandings of speculative truths.

Judgement is an identical relation between subject and predicate; in it one abstracts from the fact that the subject still has more determinations than those of the predicate, as well as from the fact that the predicate is wider than the subject.
If now the content is speculative, then the non-identity of subject and predicate is likewise an essential moment, but this is not expressed in the judgement.

The paradoxical and bizarre light in which much of the newer philosophy appears to those who have no confidence in speculative thinking falls in many ways into the form of the simple judgement, when it is used for the expression of speculative results.
zh: 这一命题因而包含着结果；它自在地就是这个结果。
然而这里需要指出的情况是这样一个缺陷：结果本身并没有在命题中被表达出来；乃是一种外在的反思在命题中认出了它。
——在这里必须立即作出那个一般性的说明：命题以判断的形式，是不适合于表达思辨的真理的；对这一情况的了解足以消除许多对思辨真理的误解。
判断是主体与谓词之间一种同一的关系；在判断中，人们撇开了主体还有着比谓词更多的规定性这一事实，也撇开了谓词比主体更宽这一事实。
但若内容是思辨的，那么主体与谓词的非同一性同样是一个本质的环节，只是这并没有在判断中被表达出来。
近代哲学中许多东西在那些不信任思辨思维的人看来所呈现出的那种悖谬而离奇的光亮，在被用来表达思辨结果时，便多方面地落入简单判断的形式之中。

en: The defect is first supplemented for the sake of expressing the speculative truth in that the opposite proposition is added, the proposition “being and nothing is not the same”, which was likewise uttered above.

But in this way a further defect arises, that these propositions are unconnected, and thus represent the content only in the antinomy, whereas their content relates to one and the same thing and the determinations expressed in the two propositions are to be united simply; — a union which can then only be expressed as an unrest at once of the incompatible, as a movement.
The most ordinary injustice done to speculative content is to make it one-sided, i.e. to single out only the one of the propositions into which it can be dissolved.

Then it cannot be denied that this proposition is being asserted; however correct the statement is, it is so false, for if once a proposition is taken from the speculative, then at the very least the other too would have to be equally considered and stated.

— Here the so-to-say unfortunate word “unity” is still especially to be mentioned; the unity signifies even more than identity a subjective reflection; it is taken above all as the relation which arises from comparison, from external reflection.

Insofar as this finds the same in two different objects, a unity is so present that the complete indifference of the objects themselves which are compared is presupposed against this unity, so that this comparing and the unity concern the objects themselves in no way and are an action and determination external to them.
The unity therefore expresses the quite abstract sameness and sounds all the harder and more striking, the more those of whom it is spoken show themselves to be simply different.
For unity one would therefore better say only indivisibility and inseparability; but thereby the affirmative of the relation of the whole is not expressed.
zh: 这一缺陷首先为了表达思辨的真理而得到如下补充：人们加上那个相反的命题，即「存在与无不是同一个东西」，这一命题上面也已经说出过。
但这样又产生了另一个缺陷：这些命题彼此没有联结，因而只是以二律背反的形式表现其内容，然而它们的内容却指向同一个东西，而在两个命题中表达的那些规定应当直接地得到统一；——而这样的统一随后只能被表达为一种同时是互不相容者的不安、一种运动。
对思辨内容所犯的最常见的错，是把它变成片面的，即只挑出那能够被分解成它的两个命题中的一个。
于是人们就不能否认这一点：人们断言的是那个命题；然而这一说明尽管正确，却是如此地错误，因为一旦一个命题被从思辨中取出，那么至少另一个命题也必须同样地得到考虑和说明。
——在这里，那个可以说是不幸的词「统一」尤其还应当被提出来；统一比同一性更多地表示一种主观的反思，它尤其被当作那种由比较、由外在反思而产生的关系。
就它在两个不同对象中发现同一个东西而言，统一是这样地存在着，以至于被比较的对象自身的完全无关紧要反倒被预设在这一统一之前；因此，这种比较与统一根本与对象自身无关，而是一种对它们而言外在地进行的做法与规定。
因此，统一表达的是完全抽象的同一；而它所谈论的那些东西越是显得纯粹地互有差别，它听起来就越是生硬而引人注目。
因此，对于统一，宁可只说不可分离性与不可分性；但这样一来，整体关系的肯定方面并没有被表达出来。

en: So the whole, true result which has here emerged is becoming, which is not merely the one-sided or abstract unity of being and nothing.

Rather it consists in this movement, that pure being is immediately and simply, that it is therefore just as much pure nothing, that the difference of the two is, but at the same time also sublates itself and is not.
The result thus asserts the difference of being and nothing just as much, but as one merely intended.
zh: 因此，这里所得出的全部的、真正的结果就是生成，它并不只是存在与无那种片面的或抽象的统一。
毋宁说，它在于这一运动：纯粹存在是直接而单纯的，因此它同样就是纯粹的无；而两者的差别是存在的，但同时又自我扬弃并且不存在。
因此，结果同样地断言存在与无的差别，但只是把它作为一个仅仅被意指的差别。

en: One thinks that being is rather the simply other than what nothing is, and nothing is clearer than their absolute difference, and nothing seems easier than to state it.
But it is just as easy to convince oneself that this is impossible, that it is unsayable.
Those who want to insist on the difference between being and nothing may be challenged to state wherein it consists.

If being and nothing had any determinateness by which they were different, then they would be, as has been remarked, determinate being and determinate nothing, not the pure being and the pure nothing which they still are here.
Their difference is therefore completely empty; each of the two is in the same way the indeterminate; it therefore does not consist in them themselves, but only in a third, in the meant.
But the meant is a form of the subjective, which does not belong to this series of exposition.
The third however, in which being and nothing have their subsistence, must also occur here; and it has also occurred here: it is becoming.
In it they are as different; becoming is only insofar as they are different.
This third is an other than they are; — they subsist only in an other, which means just as much: they do not subsist for themselves.

Becoming is the subsistence of being just as much as of non-being; or their subsistence is only their being in one; and precisely this their subsistence is what at the same time sublates their difference.
zh: 人们以为，存在毋宁是与无完全是别的东西；而它们的绝对差别再没有比这更清楚的了，要指出这个差别也再没有比这更容易的了。
但同样容易使人信服：这是不可能的，它是说不出来的。
那些想要坚持存在与无之差别的人，可以被要求指出这差别究竟何在。
如果存在与无具有某种使它们有差别的规定性，那么它们就会如前所述是被规定的存在与被规定的无，而不是它们在这里仍然是的纯粹存在与纯粹的无。
因此，它们的差别是完全空的；两者中的每一个同样都是不确定者；所以这个差别并不在它们自身之中，而只在第三者之中、只在意指之中。
但意指是主观的一种形式，它不属于这一展示的序列。
但存在与无赖以持续存在的第三者，在这里也必须出现；而它在这里也已经出现了：它就是生成。
在它之中它们作为有差别的；生成只在它们有差别的限度内存在。
这个第三者是与它们别的东西；——它们只在一个他者之中持续存在，这也就是说：它们并不是为自己而持续存在。
生成既是存在的持续存在，也是非存在的持续存在；或者说，它们的持续存在仅仅是它们在同一个之中的存在；而恰恰是它们的这一持续存在扬弃了它们的差别。

en: The demand to state the difference between being and nothing also includes within itself the saying of what being is and what nothing is.

Those who resist recognising the one as well as the other merely as a passing over into one another, and who assert this or that of being and of nothing, may state what they are speaking of, i.e. set up a definition of being and nothing and show that it is correct.

Without having satisfied this first demand of the old science — whose logical rules they otherwise accept and apply — all those assertions about being and nothing are mere pronouncements, scientific nullities.

If it has otherwise been said that existence, insofar as one initially holds it to be equivalent to being, is the supplement to possibility, then thereby another determination, possibility, is presupposed: being is not spoken of in its immediacy, even as not self-subsistent, as conditioned.
For being, which is mediated, we shall reserve the expression existence.

But one does indeed picture being to oneself — for instance under the image of pure light, as the clarity of unclouded seeing — and nothing as pure night, and ties their difference to this well-known sensuous diversity.

But in truth, if one pictures this seeing more precisely as well, one can easily perceive that in absolute clarity one sees as much and as little as in absolute darkness, that the one seeing is as good as the other, pure seeing, seeing of nothing.
Pure light and pure darkness are two empties which are the same.

Only in determinate light — and light is determined through darkness — that is, in clouded light, and equally only in determinate darkness — and darkness is determined through light — in illuminated darkness can something be distinguished, because only clouded light and illuminated darkness have the difference in themselves and are thereby determinate being, determinate existence.
zh: 要求指出存在与无的差别的这一要求，本身也就包含着要说出存在究竟是什么、无究竟是什么。
那些抗拒把存在与无仅仅看作彼此之间的过渡、并对存在与无断言这或那的人，不妨说明他们所谈的是什么，即立出一个关于存在与无的定义，并指出它是正确的。
如果没有满足旧科学的这一第一要求——他们除此之外倒是承认并运用旧科学的逻辑规则——那么所有那些关于存在与无的断言都不过是空口断言，是科学上的无效物。
如果人们曾说，存在——就人们起初把它与存在视为同义而言——乃是对可能性的补充，那么这样一来就预设了另一种规定，即可能性：存在并非在其直接性中被说出，甚至并非作为不独立者、作为有条件者被说出。
对于作为被中介者的存在，我们将把「存在」这一表述保留下来。
但人们确实会把存在设想出来——比如把它设想为纯粹之光的形象，即无遮蔽观看的明澈——而把无设想为纯粹的夜——并把二者的差别系于这一众所周知的感觉上的相异。
不过事实上，即使人们把这个观看设想得再精确一些，也很容易察觉到：在绝对的明澈中所看到的与在绝对的黑暗中所看到的一样多、一样少；一个观看与另一个观看同样好，都是纯粹的观看、对无的观看。
纯粹的光与纯粹的黑暗是两个空虚，二者是同一个。
只有在被规定的光之中——而光是通过黑暗得到规定的——也就是在混浊的光之中，同样也只有在被规定的黑暗之中——而黑暗是通过光得到规定的——在被照亮的黑暗之中，才能有某种东西被区别出来；因为唯有混浊的光与被照亮的黑暗自身就具有这一差别，并因此是被规定的存在、是定在。

en: The unity whose moments, being and nothing, are inseparable, is at the same time different from them themselves, and thus it is a third against them, which in its most peculiar form is becoming.

Passing over is the same as becoming, except that in the former the two, of which one is passed over into the other, are represented more as resting outside one another and the passing over as occurring between them.
Now wherever and however being or nothing is spoken of, this third must be present; for those do not subsist for themselves, but are only in becoming, in this third.

But this third has many empirical shapes, which are put aside or neglected by abstraction in order to hold fast its products, being and nothing, each by itself, and to show them protected against passing over.
Against such simple behaviour of abstraction it is just as simply enough to point to empirical existence, in which that abstraction itself is only a something, has a determinate existence.
Or else they are forms of reflection by which the separation of the inseparable is to be fixed.

In such a determination the opposite of itself is present in and for itself, and without going back to the nature of the matter and appealing to it, that determination of reflection is thereby confounded in itself insofar as it is taken as it presents itself and its other is shown in itself.

It would be a futile effort to want to catch all the turns and devices of reflection and its reasoning, so as to deprive it of the evasions and escapes by which it conceals its contradiction with itself and to make that impossible.

I shall therefore also refrain from taking any notice of the many so-called objections and refutations which have been raised against the proposition that neither being nor nothing is something true but only becoming is their truth; the thinking which belongs to this, to see the nullity of those refutations or rather to dislodge such devices on the spot, is brought about only by the critical cognition of the forms of understanding; but those who are most prolific in such objections at once fall upon the first sentences with their reflections, without having helped themselves or being helped, through the further study of logic, to a consciousness of the nature of these crude reflections.
zh: 那个统一——其环节即存在与无是不可分的——同时又与它们自身不同，因而它就是一个与它们相对立的第三者，而这第三者在其最特有的形式中就是生成。
过渡与生成是同一个东西，只是：在前者中，那两个——其中一个被过渡到另一个——更多地被表象为各自安顿在外，并且过渡被表象为发生在它们之间。
那么，无论在何处、以何种方式谈到存在或无，这第三者都必须在场；因为它们不是为自己而持续存在，而只是存在于生成之中、存在于这第三者之中。
但这第三者有多种经验性的形态，抽象把它们撇在一边或加以忽略，为的是把它的那些产物——存在与无——各自单独地固定下来，并把它们保护起来，使之免于被过渡。
针对抽象的这种简单的行为，同样简单地只需提醒人们注意经验的存在；在这种存在中，那个抽象本身不过是某物，它有一个定在。
或者，它们是一些反思形式，通过这些形式，那不可分者的分离将被固定下来。
在这样的规定中，其自身的反面自在地就在场；而无需回到事情的本性并向它诉求，那一反思规定就因如下这一点而在自身上被混淆了：它被照它所呈现的样子取用，而它的他者在它自身上被指了出来。
想把反思及其推理议论的一切转折与机巧统统抓住，以便剥夺它那些用来掩盖其自身矛盾的托辞与遁路、并使这种掩盖成为不可能，这将是徒劳的努力。
因此我也不去顾及那些被提出来反对「存在与无都不是什么真者、唯有生成才是它们的真理」这一命题的众多所谓异议与反驳；要看出那些反驳的无效性、或者毋宁说当场把这些机巧驱走，那种属于此的思维活动，只能通过对知性诸形式的批判性认识来实现；而那些在这类异议上最为多产的人，一上手就用他们的反思扑向最初的几句话，并没有通过进一步研究逻辑学而使自己获得、或者帮助自己获得对这些粗陋反思之性质的认识。

en: Some of the phenomena which result therefrom are to be considered, namely when being and nothing are isolated from one another and one is placed outside the range of the other, so that passing over is thereby negated.
zh: 应当考察由此产生的若干现象：当存在与无被彼此孤立开来、其中一个被置于另一个的范围之外时，情形便是如此——由此过渡就被否定了。

en: Parmenides held fast to being and was the most consistent, in that he at the same time said of nothing that it is not at all, that only being is.

Being, quite by itself, is the indeterminate; it therefore has no relation to the other; it thus appears that no further progress can be made from this beginning, namely from itself, and that progress can occur only by something foreign being knotted on to it from outside.
The progress that being is the same as nothing thus appears as a second, absolute beginning, — a passing over which is for itself and comes externally to being.
Being would not be the absolute beginning at all if it had a determinateness; in that case it would depend on an other and would not be immediate, would not be the beginning.
But if it is indeterminate and thereby the true beginning, it also has nothing by which it passes over to an other; it is at the same time the end.
As little as anything can break out of it, so too nothing can break in into it; in Parmenides as in Spinoza one is not to go on from being or the absolute substance to the negative, the finite.
Now if progress is nevertheless made — which, as noted, can happen only in an external way from the relationless, and thus progressless being — then this progress is a second, new beginning.

Thus Fichte’s most absolute, unconditional principle is: A = A, positing; the second is counter-positing; this is to be in part conditioned, in part unconditional (and so the contradiction in itself).

This is a proceeding of external reflection which just as much negates again that with which it begins as an absolute — the counter-positing is the negation of the first identity — as it makes its second unconditional explicitly at once into a conditioned one.

But if there were in general a justification for going forward, i.e. for subverting the first beginning, then it would have to lie in this first itself that an other could relate itself to it; it would thus have to be a determinate [being].
But being, or the absolute substance, does not present itself as such; on the contrary.
It is the immediate, that which is still simply indeterminate.
zh: 巴门尼德坚持存在，并且最为彻底：因为他同时说到无时说，它根本不存在，唯有存在是存在着的。
完全独自的存在乃是不确定者，因而对他者没有任何关系；于是似乎，从这个开端出发不能进一步前进，即不能从它自身出发继续前进，而前进只能是这样发生的：从外面把某种陌生的东西系结到它上面。
于是，「存在与无是同一个东西」这一推进显现为第二个、绝对的开端——一个自在的、外在地添加到存在之上的过渡。
如果存在具有某种规定性，那么存在总体上就不会是绝对的开端；那时它就依赖于一个他者，不再是直接者，也就不再是开端。
但如果它是不确定的，因而是真正的开端，那么它也没有任何东西可借以过渡到一个他者；它同时就是终点。
正如没有什么能够从它里面冲出来一样，也没有什么能够闯进它里面；在巴门尼德那里，在斯宾诺莎那里，人们都不应当从存在或绝对实体继续前进到否定者、有限者。
然而若仍然继续前进——如前所述，这只能从那个没有关系、因而不能前进的存在出发，以纯粹外在的方式发生——那么这一推进就是第二个、新的开端。
于是，费希特的绝对最无条件的原则是：A = A 设定；第二个是对立设定；后者应当一部分是有条件的、一部分是无条件的（因而自在地就包含着矛盾）。
这是外在反思的一种推进：它既重新否定它作为绝对者所由之开始的那个东西——对立设定乃是对第一个同一性的否定——又同时立刻把它的第二个无条件的者明确地变成一个有条件的者。
但如果总归存在一种继续前进的正当理由，即扬弃第一个开端，那么这就必须在于这个最初者自身之中：他者能够与之相关；因此它就必须是一个被规定者。
然而，存在乃至绝对实体并不以这样的身分显现出来；恰恰相反。
它是直接者，是那个还纯粹地不确定的东西。

en: The most eloquent, perhaps forgotten, descriptions of the impossibility of getting from an abstract to something more remote and to a unification of the two are given by Jacobi in the interest of his polemic against the Kantian synthesis of self-consciousness a priori in his essay On the Enterprise of Bringing Reason to Understanding by Criticism (Works, III.
Bd.).

He poses the task (S. 113) in such a way that in something pure, whether it be of consciousness, of space or of time, the arising or production of a synthesis is to be shown. “Space shall be One, time shall be One, consciousness shall be One.”

Just tell how one of these three Ones multiplies itself purely within itself, ... each is only One and no other; a sameness of One, a self-sameness of the-this-that! without this-ness, that-ness, such-ness; for these slumber with the this, that, such yet in the infinite = 0 of the indeterminate, out of which everything and every determinate is first to emerge!
What brings... into those three infinities...
Finitude; what impregnates space and time a priori with number and measure and transforms them into a pure multiplicity; what brings pure spontaneity (the I) to oscillation...?
How does its pure vowel come to a consonant, or rather how does its silent, uninterrupted blowing, interrupting itself, set itself down, in order to gain at least a kind of self-sound, an accent?

“— One sees that Jacobi has very clearly recognised the non-being of abstraction, be it the so-called absolute, i.e. merely abstract space, or just such time, or just such pure consciousness, the I; he persists in this in order to assert the impossibility of a progression to an other, the condition of a synthesis, and of the synthesis itself.

The synthesis which constitutes the interest must not be taken as a linkage of determinations already existing externally, — partly the business is itself the production of a second to a first, of a determinate to the indeterminate primordial [beginning], partly however it is the immanent synthesis, synthesis a priori, — the unity of those different in themselves subsisting in and for itself.

Becoming is this immanent synthesis of being and nothing; but because for synthesis the sense of an external coming-together of what exists externally opposite one another lies nearest to hand, the name synthesis, synthetic unity, has rightly been put out of use.
— Jacobi asks: how does the pure vowel of the I come to a consonant, what brings determinateness into indeterminateness?

The what? would be easily answered, and Kant has answered this question in his own way; but the question as to the how? means: in what manner and way, according to what relation and the like, and so demands the specification of a particular category; but of manner and way, of categories of understanding, there can be no question here.

The question as to the how? itself belongs to the bad habits of reflection, which asks about intelligibility, but in doing so presupposes its fixed categories and thereby knows itself to be armed in advance against the answering of that about which it asks.

Neither does it have, with Jacobi, the higher sense of a question about the necessity of the synthesis; for, as said, he remains firmly insisting on the abstractions, for the assertion of the impossibility of the synthesis.

In particular he describes vividly (S. 147) the procedure for arriving at the abstraction of space: “I must... for so long seek purely to forget that I ever saw, heard, felt and touched anything whatever, myself expressly not excepted.
Purely, purely, purely must I forget all motion and leave to me precisely this forgetting, because it is the hardest thing, most earnestly to be careful about.

Everything whatever must I, just as I have thought it away, have completely and entirely removed too, and leave nothing remaining except the forcibly surviving intuition of the infinite, unchangeable space alone.

I may therefore also not think myself back into it again as something different from it and yet bound to it; I may not merely let myself be surrounded and penetrated by it, but I must pass over completely into it, become one with it, transform myself into it; I must leave nothing of myself remaining except this my intuition itself, in order to consider it as a truly independent, non-dependent, single and sole representation.”
zh: 关于不可能从一个抽象者走向某个更远者、走向二者的统一的最雄辩的、也许已被遗忘的描述，是雅各布在其《论通过批判把理性带入知性的事业》一文中、为其反对康德关于自我意识之 a priori 综合的论战目的而给出的（著作集，III.
Bd.）。
他这样提出问题（S. 113）：在某个纯粹者中——无论是意识的、空间的还是时间的——应当展示出某种综合的产生或造就。「空间是一，时间是一，意识是一。
只须说说，这三者之一如何在它自身之中纯粹地自我增殖……每一个都只是一，不是别的东西；一种一的同一，一种这个—那个—那一个的自身同一！没有这个性、那个性、那一个性；因为这些与这个、那个、那一个一起还沉睡在不确定者的无限 = 0 之中，一切和每个规定者也都首先应当从那里产生出来！
是什么把……带进那三个无限者之中……
有限性；是什么 a priori 地以数与度使空间与时间受精，并把它们转化为纯粹的多样性；是什么使纯粹的自发性（我）进入振荡……？
它那纯粹的母音怎会变成辅音；或者毋宁说，它那无声的、不间断的吹气——在打断自己时——如何停下来，以便至少赢得某种自身之音、一个重音？
」——人们看到，雅各布已十分明确地认出了抽象的非存在，无论它是指所谓的绝对者，即仅仅抽象的空间，还是同样抽象的时间，抑或同样抽象的纯粹意识、我；他坚持这一点，为的是断言：不存在向一个他者——即综合的条件——的推进，也断言综合本身是不可能的。
那个构成这一兴趣所在的综合，不应当被看作外在已经存在的诸规定之间的联结——部分地，它所涉及的正是为一个最初者产生出第二者、为一个不确定的开端产生出一个被规定者；部分地，它所涉及的却是内在的综合、综合 a priori——那些自在地存在着的、彼此有差别的者的统一。
生成就是存在与无的这种内在综合；但由于就综合而言，最切近的是那种「外在的、彼此相对而现成的东西相互结合起来」的含义，所以「综合」「综合性的统一」这个名称被正当地弃用了。
——雅各布问道：「我」的纯粹母音怎会变成辅音，是什么把规定性带进不确定性之中？
「是什么？」倒容易回答，康德已经以他自己的方式回答了这个问题；但「怎样？」这个问题意味着：以何种方式、按何种关系等等，因此它要求指明一个特殊的范畴；然而这里所涉及的并不是方式方法，也不是知性的诸范畴。
「怎样？」这个问题本身就属于反思的坏习惯：反思追问可理解性，却在此同时预设自己固定的范畴，因而它自知已经预先武装起来，以防备对那个它所追问的东西的回答。
在雅各布那里，它同样也没有那种关于综合之必然性的问题的更高意义；因为如前所说，他仍然固执地坚持那些抽象，为的是断言综合的不可能性。
他尤其形象地描述了（S. 147）达到对空间的抽象的程序：「我必须……在这段时间里努力纯粹地忘掉：我曾经看见、听见、触动和摸到过任何东西——我自己明确地不算在内。
我必须纯粹地、纯粹地、纯粹地忘掉一切运动；而这个忘掉本身，因为它是最难的事，恰恰是最需要加以留意的。
一切东西总之，我既已在思惟中把它消除，就也必须让它被完全而彻底地清除掉，除了那凭强力留存下来的、对无限而不变的空间的单纯直观之外，什么也不留下。
因此，我也不得再把自己重新设想进它里面、设想成某种与它有差别却又与它相连的东西；我不得只是让自己被它包围和贯穿，而必须完全过渡到它之中，与它合为一体，把自己转化为它；我必须不给自己留下任何东西，除了这同一个直观本身，以便把它看作一个真正独立的、无所依赖的、统一而唯一的表象。」

en: With this wholly abstract purity of continuity, i.e. indeterminateness and emptiness of representing, it is indifferent whether one calls this abstraction space or pure intuition, pure thinking; — it is all the same as what the Indian — when, externally motionless and equally without motion in sensation, representation, fantasy, desire etc., he looks year-long only at the tip of his nose, says inwardly to himself only Om, Om, Om or nothing at all — calls Brahma.
This dull, empty consciousness, taken as consciousness, is being.
zh: 在这种完全抽象的连续性的纯粹性中，即在表象活动的不确定性与空虚中，把这一抽象叫做空间也好，叫做纯粹直观、纯粹思维也好，都是无关紧要的；——那个印度人——当他在外面毫无动静、在感觉、表象、幻想、欲望等等方面同样纹丝不动地长年只盯着自己的鼻尖、内在对自己只念着「Om, Om, Om」或者什么也不说的时候——称作梵（Brahma）的东西，与这一切完全是一回事。
这个迟钝的、空的意识，一旦作为意识来把握，就是存在。

en: In this emptiness, Jacobi now continues, the opposite happens to him of what, according to Kant’s assurance, should happen to him; he finds himself not as a many and multiplicity, but rather as One without all plurality and multiplicity; yes, “I am the impossibility itself, I am the annihilation of all multiplicity and plurality, ... I cannot restore the least of that from my purely, altogether simple, unchangeable essence, nor engulf it in myself ...
Thus everything outside-ness and alongside-ness, all multiplicity and plurality that rests solely on this being-outside-and-alongside, reveals itself (in this purity) as something purely impossible.”
zh: 雅各布继续说：在这片空虚中，降临在他身上的恰是按照康德的断言本应降临在他身上的那个东西的反面；他发现自己是作为一、作为没有一切众多与多样性的一个而存在，而非作为众多与多样；是的，「我本身就是这种不可能性，我本身就是一切多样与众多的毁灭……我无法从我的纯粹、绝对单纯、不变的本质中恢复出那东西的丝毫，也不能把它吞入我之中……
于是（在这种纯粹性中）……一切在外与并列、仅仅建立在这一在外与并列之上的全部多样性与众多性，都显现为纯粹的不可能。」

en: This impossibility means nothing other than the tautology: I hold fast to the abstract unity and exclude all plurality and multiplicity, I hold fast to the difference-less and the indeterminate, and I look away from everything different and determinate.
The Kantian synthesis a priori of self-consciousness, i.e. the activity of this unity to determine itself and in this determination to maintain itself, Jacobi dilutes into the same abstraction.
That “synthesis in itself”, that “original judging”, he makes one-sidedly into “the copula in itself, — an is, is, is, without beginning and end and without what, who and which”.
This repetition of the repetition which goes on to infinity is the sole activity, function and production of the very purest synthesis; it itself is the mere, pure, absolute repetition itself”.
Or in truth, since there is no paragraph, i.e. no negation, no distinguishing in it, so it is not a repetition, but only the undifferentiated simple being.
— But is this still synthesis, when Jacobi precisely leaves out that by which the unity is synthetic unity?
zh: 这种不可能无非就是那个同义反复：我坚持抽象的统一、排除一切众多与多样性，我坚持那无差别的与不确定的，并且从一切有差别的与被规定者那里把目光移开。
康德关于自我意识之 a priori 综合，即这一统一以规定自身、并在这一规定中保持自身的活动，被雅各布稀释成了同一个抽象。
那个「自在的综合」、那个「原初的判断」，他片面地变成了「自在的系词——一个是、是、是，没有开端与终结，也没有何、谁与哪一者。
这种不断趋向无限的「重复的重复」，乃是最纯粹的综合唯一的活动、功能与生产；它本身就是那个单纯的、纯粹的、绝对的重复本身」。
或者说事实上，由于其中没有段落，即没有否定、没有区别，所以它不是一种重复，而只是那无差别的单纯存在。
——但当雅各布恰恰撇下了那个使统一成为综合性的统一的东西时，这还算综合吗？

en: First, if Jacobi thus establishes himself in the absolute, i.e. abstract space, time, also consciousness, one has to say that he thereby transfers and holds himself to something empirically false; there is, i.e. empirically present is no space and time which would be an unlimited spatial and temporal something, not filled in their continuity with a manifold of determinate existence and change, so that these limits and changes belong undivided and inseparably to spatiality and temporality; likewise consciousness is filled with determinate feeling, representing, desiring etc.; it does not exist separated from any particular content.

— Empirical passing over explains itself of course; consciousness may indeed make the empty space, empty time and the empty consciousness itself, or pure being, its object and content; but it does not stop there; rather than merely going beyond, it presses out of such emptiness towards something better, i.e. towards content more concrete in some way; and however bad a content may otherwise be, in this respect it is better and truer; precisely such a content is a synthetic one in general; taken synthetically in the more general sense.
Thus Parmenides has to do with appearance and opinion, the opposite of being and truth; so Spinoza with the attributes, the modes, extension, movement, understanding, will etc.
The synthesis contains and shows the untruth of those abstractions; in it they are at one with their other, thus not as subsisting for themselves, not as absolute, but simply as relative.
zh: 首先，如果雅各布这样把自己安置在绝对的、即抽象的空间、时间以及意识之中，那么人们就得说：他是这样把自己搬到了并且固定在一个经验上虚假的东西上；并不存在——也就是说，经验上并不存在——这样的空间和时间，它们会是一种无界限的空间者与时间者，会在其连续性中不由多样地受限制的定在与变化所充满，以致这些界限与变化不可分、不可分离地属于空间性与时间性；同样，意识也由规定的感受、表象、欲求等等所充满；它并不是与任何特殊内容相分离而存在的。
——经验的过渡本来就不言自明；意识固然可以把空的空间、空的时间、空的意识本身或者纯粹存在当作自己的对象与内容；但它并不停留于此，而是并不只是走出去，而是从这种空虚中挤向一个更好的、也就是以某种方式更为具体的内容；而一个内容无论原本多么糟糕，就这一点而言它却是更好、更真的；恰恰这样一个内容总归是一个综合性的内容；在更一般的意义上被当作综合性的。
于是巴门尼德不得不与假象和意见——即存在与真理的对立面——打交道；斯宾诺莎则不得不与诸属性、诸样式、广延、运动、知性、意志等等打交道。
综合包含并展示出那些抽象的非真；在其中，它们与其自身之他者相统一，因此不是作为为自己而存在者、不是作为绝对者，而纯属相对者。

en: But the showing of the empirical nullity of empty space etc. is not what it is about.
Consciousness can indeed, by abstracting, also fill itself with that indeterminate, and the abstractions held fast are the thoughts of pure space, pure time, pure consciousness, pure being.

The thought of pure space etc., i.e. pure space etc. in itself, is to be shown as null, i.e. that as such it is already its opposite, that already its opposite has penetrated into it, that it is already for itself the going-out-of-itself, determinateness.
zh: 但指出空的空间等等的经验上的无效性，却不是问题之所在。
意识固然也可以通过抽象而以那个不确定者充实自身，而被固定下来的那些抽象就是关于纯粹空间、纯粹时间、纯粹意识、纯粹存在的思想。
关于纯粹空间等等的思想，即纯粹空间等等自身，应当被指出为无效的，也就是：它作为这样的东西已经是它的对立面，它自身的对立面已经渗入其中，它已经为自己就是那种出自自身的走出，即规定性。

en: But this results immediately from them.
They are, as Jacobi describes at length, results of abstraction, are expressly determined as the indeterminate, which — to go back to its simplest form — is being.

But precisely this indeterminateness is what constitutes the determinateness of it; for indeterminateness is the opposite of determinateness; it is thus as the opposite itself the determinate or the negative, and indeed the pure, quite abstract negative.

This indeterminateness or abstract negation, which thus has being in itself, is what the external as well as the internal reflection expresses, in that it equates it with nothing, declares it an empty thing of thought, nothing.
— Or, so it can be put, because being is the determination-less, it is not the (affirmative) determinateness that it is, not being, but nothing.
zh: 但这一点直接从它们自身就可以得出。
它们——正如雅各布详尽描述的那样——是抽象的结果，被明确地规定为不确定者，而这个——若回到其最简单的形式——就是存在。
但恰恰是这种不确定性构成了它的规定性；因为不确定性是与规定性相对立的；因此它作为对立者本身就是规定者或否定者，而且恰恰是纯粹的、完全抽象的否定者。
这种不确定性或者说抽象的否定（它正是这样在自身中具有存在的），乃是外在的反思与内在的反思所表达出来的东西：它们把它等同于无，宣布它是一个空的思想物、就是无。
——或者说可以这样表述：因为存在乃是无规定者，所以它并不是它所是的那个（肯定的）规定性，不是存在，而是无。

en: In the pure reflection of the beginning, as it is made in this logic with being as such, the transition is still hidden; because being is only posited as immediate, nothing breaks out of it only immediately.

But all the following determinations, such as determinate existence itself, are more concrete; in it that is already posited which contains and brings forth the contradiction of those abstractions and hence their passing over.

With being as that simple, immediate [one], the reminder that it is the result of complete abstraction, thus already on that account abstract negativity, nothing, is left behind by the science, which within itself, expressly starting from essence, will present that one-sided immediacy as a mediated one, where being is posited as existence and the mediating of this being, the ground, is posited.
zh: 在对开端的纯粹反思中——在这门逻辑学里这个开端是与作为这样的存在一同作出的——那个过渡仍然被隐藏着；因为存在只是作为直接者被设定的，所以无也只是直接地从它里面冲出来。
但一切随后的规定——例如定在本身——都更为具体；在定在之中，那个包含着那些抽象的矛盾、因而也包含着它们的过渡的东西，已经被设定了。
当存在作为那个单纯者、直接者时，那个提醒——即存在是完全抽象的结果，因而本身就已经是抽象的否定性、就是无——被科学抛在身后；科学将在其自身之内、明确地从本质出发，把那种片面的直接性表现为一种被中介的直接性，在那里存在被设定为存在，而这一存在的中介者、那个根据，则被设定。

en: With that reminder the transition from being into nothing can be pictured or, as one says, explained and made comprehensible as something itself easy and trivial: namely that being, which has been made the beginning of the science, is nothing, for one can abstract from everything, and when everything has been abstracted from, nothing remains.
But one may continue: thus the beginning is not an affirmative, not being, but simply nothing, and nothing is then also the end, at least as much as the immediate being and even much more.
The shortest course is to let such reasoning have its way and to look at how the results are constituted on which it insists.

That accordingly nothing would be the result of that reasoning and the beginning should now be made with nothing (as in Chinese philosophy) would be no reason for turning the hand, for before one turned it, this nothing would just as well have turned into being (see above: B. Nothing).

But further, if that abstraction from everything, which is after all something that is, were presupposed, it is to be taken more precisely; the result of the abstraction from everything that is is at first abstract being, being in general; as in the cosmological proof of the existence of God, from the contingent being of the world, over which one thereby rises, being is still carried up, being is determined to infinite being.
But one can indeed also abstract from this pure being, the being can still be struck up to the All from which it has already been abstracted; then nothing remains.

One can now, if one wants to forget the thinking of nothing, i.e. its turning into being, or knows nothing of it, continue in the style of that ability; for (thank God!) one can also abstract from nothing (as indeed the creation of the world is an abstraction from nothing), and then it is not nothing that remains, for it is precisely from this that one abstracts, but one has thus arrived back in being.
— This ability gives an external play of abstracting, whereby abstracting itself is only the one-sided doing of the negative.

First of all, it lies in this ability itself that being is as indifferent to it as nothing, and that as much as each of the two disappears, so much does each also arise; but it is just as indifferent whether one starts from the doing of nothing or from nothing; the doing of nothing, i.e. mere abstracting, is no more and no less something true than mere nothing.
zh: 有了那个提醒，从存在到无的过渡就可以被设想为、或者像人们所说的那样被解释、被弄得可以理解，而且它本身就是一件容易而平淡的事：即那个被当作科学开头的存在乃是无，因为人们可以从一切事物抽象掉，而当从一切事物抽象掉之后，剩下的就是无。
但人们可以继续说：那么，开端就不是一个肯定者，不是存在，而恰恰就是无；而无于是也就是终点，至少与直接的存在一样，甚至还要更多。
最省事的做法是让这种推理议论自行其是，并看一看它所坚持的那些结果究竟是怎样构成的。
那么，无就会是那种推理议论的结果、开端就该用无来作成（如同在中国哲学中那样），这固然不构成掉转手来的理由，因为在掉转它之前，这个无同样地早就已经变成了存在（见上：B. 无）。
但进一步说，如果那种从一切——而一切毕竟是存在者——的抽象被预设了，那么它就应当被更精确地把握；从一切存在者抽象出来的结果，首先是抽象的存在、一般的存在；如同在上帝的存在的宇宙论证明中那样，人们从世界的偶然存在——在那里人们正是从它上升而起的——还把存在一并带了上来，把存在规定为无限的存在。
不过，人们固然也可以从这一纯粹的存在抽象出来，存在还可以被提升到那个已经从之抽象掉的一切者之上；那么剩下的就是无。
人们现在可以——如果人们想要忘掉对无的思维，即无向存在的翻转，或者对此一无所知——按照那种「能」的样式继续下去；因为（感谢上帝！）也可以从无抽象出来（世界的创造同样也是从无的一种抽象），于是剩下的并不是无，因为恰恰是从这个无抽象出来的，而是人们就这样又回到了存在之中。
——这种「能」给出的是一场抽象化的外在游戏，其中抽象化本身只是否定者的片面的作为。
首先，这一「能」本身就包含着：对它来说，存在与无同样无关紧要；而两者中的每一个在消失多少的时候，也就同样产生多少；但同样无关紧要的是，人们是从无的作为出发还是从无出发；无的作为，即单纯的抽象化，并不比单纯的无更多，也不比它更少地是某种真者。

en: The dialectic according to which Plato treats the One in the Parmenides must likewise be taken more for a dialectic of external reflection.
Being and the One are both Eleatic forms which are the same.
But they are also to be distinguished; Plato takes them so in that dialogue.

After he has removed from the One the manifold determinations of being whole and part, of being in itself, of being in an other etc., of figure, time etc., the result is that being does not accrue to the One, for otherwise being would accrue to a something only according to one of those ways (Steph.

Thereupon Plato treats the proposition “the One is”, and one has to see in him how the transition to the non-being of the One is brought about; it happens through the comparison of the two determinations of the presupposed proposition: “the One is”, it contains the One and being, and “the One is” contains more than when one says only: “the One”.
In the fact that they are different, the moment of negation which the proposition contains is shown.
It is evident that this path has a presupposition and is an external reflection.
zh: 柏拉图在《巴门尼德篇》中据以处理一者的辩证法，同样也应更多地被看作外在反思的辩证法。
存在与一者都是爱利亚学派的两种形式，二者是同一个东西。
但它们也必须加以区别；柏拉图在那篇对话中就是这样取用的。
在他从一者那里去掉了关于整体与部分、关于自身之内、关于在他者之中的种种规定，以及关于形状、时间等等的规定之后，结果就是：存在并不归属于一者；因为否则，存在只有按照那些方式之一才归属于某物（Steph.
于是柏拉图处理那个命题：「一者存在」，而人们得在他那里考察：从这个命题出发，向一者的非存在的过渡是如何被作成的；这是通过对那个预设命题的两个规定的比较而发生的：「一者存在」，它包含着一者与存在；而「一者存在」比人们只说「一者」包含着更多。
正是在它们彼此不同这一点上，命题所包含的否定的环节被指了出来。
显然，这条道路有一个预设，并且是一种外在的反思。

en: As here the One is put in connection with being, so being, which is to be held fast for itself abstractly, is shown most simply, without entering into thinking, in a connection which contains the opposite of what is to be asserted.
Being, taken as it is immediately, belongs to a subject; it is something uttered, has an empirical determinate existence in general, and thereby stands on the ground of the limit and of the negative.

In whatever expressions or turns the understanding puts itself when it resists the unity of being and nothing and appeals to what is immediately present, it will find precisely in this experience nothing but determinate being, being with a limit or negation, — that very unity which it rejects.
The assertion of immediate being thus reduces itself to an empirical existence whose showing it cannot reject, because it is the immediacy outside of thinking to which it wants to hold.
zh: 正如同这里一者被与存在置于联结之中，那个应当自在地、抽象地被固定下来的存在，最简单地、而不必进入思维，就被展示在一个联结之中，而这个联结包含着与那应当被断言的东西相对立的一面。
存在，就它直接的样子来把握，属于一个主体；它是一个被说出的东西，一般地有一个经验上的定在，并因此站在界限与否定者的地基上。
当知性抗拒存在与无的统一、并援引那直接现成的东西时，无论它用什么样的表达或说法把自己表述出来，它在这项经验中恰恰只会发现被规定的存在、带有一个界限或否定的存在——也就是它所拒斥的那个统一。
于是，对直接存在的断言就归结为一种经验的存在；而对它的展示是无法被拒斥的，因为这种断言所要持守的，正是思维之外的直接性。

en: The same is the case with nothing, only in the opposite way, and this reflection has been made about it often enough and is well known.
Nothing, taken in its immediacy, shows itself as being, for according to its nature it is the same as being.
Nothing is thought, represented, it is spoken of; it is therefore; the nothing has its being in thinking, representing, speaking etc.

But this being is further also distinguished from it; it is therefore said that nothing is indeed in thinking, representing, but that it is not thereby itself, that being does not accrue to it as such, that only thinking or representing is this being.
In this distinguishing it is just as little to be denied that nothing looks toward a being; but in the relation — whether it also contains the difference — a unity with being is present.
In whatever way nothing is uttered or shown, it shows itself in connection with — or, if one will, touching — a being, undivided from a being, precisely in a determinate existence.
zh: 对无来说情形也是一样，只是采取相反的方式；而关于无的这种反思，人们已经做得足够多、也早已人所共知了。
无，就其直接性来把握，显现为存在着的；因为按其本性，它与存在是同一个东西。
无被思维、被表象，人们谈论它，所以它是存在着的；无在思维、表象、言说等等之中有其存在。
但这存在又进一步与它相区别；因此人们说：固然无是在思维、在表象之中，但无并不因此就是它自己，存在并不作为这样的东西归属于它，这个存在只是思维或表象。
在这一区别中，同样不可否认的是：无是朝向一个存在而看的；但在这种关系中——无论它是否也包含着这一差别——都存在着与存在的统一。
无论无以何种方式被说出或被展示，它都是在与一个存在的联结中——或者说，在与一个存在的接触中——显现出来的，与一个存在不可分，正是在一个定在之中。

en: But when nothing is thus shown in a determinate existence, this difference of it from being is usually still present to the mind: that the determinate existence of nothing is in no respect anything that accrues to it itself, that it does not have being in itself for itself, that it is not being as such, that nothing is only the absence of being, darkness thus only the absence of light, cold only the absence of warmth etc.

Darkness has meaning only in relation to the eye, in external comparison with the positive, with light; cold likewise is only something in our sensation; light, warmth like being on the contrary are for themselves the objective, the real, the effective, of an altogether different quality and dignity than those negatives, than nothing.
One often finds it presented as a very important reflection and significant insight that darkness is only the absence of light, cold only the absence of warmth.

About this ingenious reflection it can be observed empirically in this field of empirical objects that darkness indeed shows itself effective in light, in that it determines the latter as colour and thereby first grants it visibility, in that, as said earlier, in pure light just as little is seen as in pure darkness.

But visibility is effectiveness in the eye, in which that negative has just as much part as the light which holds for the real, the positive; likewise the cold gives itself sufficiently recognisable to the water, to our sensation etc., and if we deny it the so-called objective reality, nothing at all is thereby gained against it.

But further it would have to be censured that here too, as above, one speaks of a negative of determinate content, does not stop at nothing itself, which in its empty abstraction does not fall short of being nor has anything before it.

— But cold, darkness and such determinate negations are to be taken at once for themselves, and one has to see what is thereby posited with a view to their general determination, according to which they are brought here.
They are not to be nothing in general, but the nothing of light, of warmth etc., of something determinate, of a content; thus they are determinate, contentful nothings, if one may say so.
But a determinateness is, as will appear further on, itself a negation; thus they are negative nothings; but a negative nothing is something affirmative.

The turning of nothing through its determinateness (which just now appeared as a determinate existence in the subject, or in whatever else it may be) into an affirmative appears to the consciousness which stands firm in the abstraction of understanding as the most paradoxical; as simple as the insight is — or because of its very simplicity the insight that the negation of the negation is positive itself appears as something trivial, on which the proud understanding therefore need take no notice, though the matter is correct, — and it has not only this correctness, but, for the sake of the universality of such determinations, its infinite extension and general application, so that one would indeed have to take notice of it.
zh: 但当无这样在一个定在之中被展示出来时，它与存在之间的这一差别通常仍然萦绕在人们心头：以为无的定在绝不是任何归属于它自己的东西，以为它自身并不具有那为自己的存在，以为它并不是作为这样的存在，以为无只是存在的缺席，黑暗如此也只是光的缺席，寒冷也只是温暖的缺席，等等。
人们说：黑暗只有在与眼睛相关联时才有意义，在与肯定者、即光的纯粹外在比较中才有意义；同样，寒冷只是我们感受中的某种东西；相反，光、温暖以及存在则是自在地作为客观者、实在者、生效者，具有与那些否定者、与无完全不同的质与尊严。
人们常常发现，人们把「黑暗只是光的缺席、寒冷只是温暖的缺席」当作一项极为重要的反思和一个有意义的认识提出来。
关于这个敏锐的反思，在经验对象的这一领域里可以经验地观察到：黑暗在光之中确实显示出其效力，因为它把光规定为颜色，并由此首先赋予光以可见性；因为正如前面所说的，在纯粹的光中所看到的，与在纯粹的黑暗中同样少。
但可见性乃是眼睛中的效力，而那个否定者在其中与那对于实在者、肯定者有效的光具有同样多的参与；同样，寒冷也向水、向我们的感受等等充分地显露出自己，而如果我们否认它那所谓的客观实在性，那么我们对此并没有赢得任何东西。
但进一步还应当责难的是：这里同样如上，人们谈论的是一个有规定内容的否定者，并没有停留在无本身；而这个无在其空洞的抽象中既不欠缺于存在，也没有任何东西在它之前。
——但寒冷、黑暗以及诸如此类的有规定的否定者应当立即被单独地把握，并且应当看清：按照它们被带到这里来的那一普遍规定，就此而言，它们被设定了什么。
它们不应是一般意义上的无，而应当是相对于光、温暖等等、相对于某个被规定者、某个内容而言的无；这样，如果可以这样说的话，它们就是有规定、有内容的无。
但一种规定性——正如后面还会出现的那样——本身就是一种否定；因此它们是否定的无；但否定的无乃是某种肯定者。

无通过其规定性（这一规定性刚才曾显现为主体之中的一个定在、或者别的什么中的定在）向肯定者的翻转，对于那个固守在知性抽象之中的意识来说显得是最为悖谬的；「否定之否定是肯定」这一洞见是如此简单，或者说，由于它自身的简单，这一洞见显得是某种平淡无奇的东西，是那骄傲的知性因而无需加以注意的东西——尽管这件事是有其正确性的；——而它不仅有这份正确性，而且由于这类规定的普遍性，还有它无限的展开与普遍的应用，因此大概倒是应当对它加以注意的。

en: One can further remark about the determination of the transition of being and nothing into one another that it is likewise to be apprehended without any further determination of reflection.

It is immediate and quite abstract, for the sake of the abstraction of the passing-over moments, i.e. in that the determinateness of the other is not yet posited in these moments, by virtue of which they passed over; nothing is not yet posited in being, although being is essentially nothing and conversely.
It is therefore inadmissible to apply further determinate mediations here and to take being and nothing in any relation, — that passing over is not yet a relation.

It is therefore improper to say: “Nothing is the ground of being” or “being is the ground of nothing”, “nothing is the cause of being” etc.; or “it can only pass over into nothing on the condition that something is, or into being only on the condition of non-being.”
The manner of the relation cannot be further determined without the related sides being further determined at the same time.

The connection of ground and consequence etc. no longer has the mere being and nothing as the sides which it connects, but expressly being, which is ground, and something which is indeed only a posited [being], not a self-subsisting one, but which is not the abstract nothing.
zh: 关于存在与无彼此之间的过渡的规定，还可以指出：它同样应当不经任何进一步的反思规定来把握。
它是直接的、完全抽象的，这是为了那些被过渡的环节之抽象的缘故，也就是：在于这些环节上还没有设定另一个的规定性、它们正是凭借这一规定性而过渡了；无还没有被设定在存在上，尽管存在在本质上就是无，反之亦然。
因此，在这里进一步应用有规定的中介、并把存在与无置于某种关系之中，都是不允许的——那个过渡还不是一种关系。
因此，说「无是存在的根据」或「存在是无的根据」、「无是存在的原因」等等，都是不许可的；或者说「只有在某物存在的条件下才过渡到无，或者只有在非存在的条件下才过渡到存在」，也是不许可的。
这种关系的方式不可能被进一步规定，而不同时进一步规定那被联结的两方。
根据与后果等等的联结，不再以单纯的存在与无作为它所联结的两方，而是明确地以作为根据的存在，以及某种固然只是一个被设定者、一个不独立者、但却不是抽象的无的东西作为两方。
